content.text: Hell yes. Diagnose why the wrong-partner test flags independent controls. Fix and qualify it on controls before touching the manuscript again, freeze the rules, and keep the failures in the receipts. 🐍

items.text: I’ll keep the manuscript scores untouched while I diagnose the control failure. Then I’ll freeze a revised wrong-partner test and qualify it on synthetic controls, with the failed v21 procedure preserved for comparison. 🐍

The old test has a structural problem: “true partner beats wrong partner” can happen even when the word choices are independent. Partner leaves can share word families and sample sizes, and the model can transfer its own estimation errors between them.

I’m separating those effects with synthetic data. The revised test will compare against shuffled data that preserves those features and refits the model each time, so a positive raw gain alone won’t count as evidence. 🐍

items.text:
The ablation found a concrete cause. On 100 independent H-stream controls, the fixed-model version gives a positive raw advantage in 98 cases. Using the known generating rates to centre donor residuals cuts that to 53; the mean gain falls from about .00223 to .00006 bits.

So much of the apparent advantage is shared model error. I’m freezing a refit-and-shuffle test, then checking its false positives and planted-signal sensitivity on separate control seeds. The manuscript remains unscored.

items.text:
The revised shuffle test passes the independent-word controls: 39 of 800 are flagged, and it detects all 48 strong plants.

But the stress test caught another boundary: when each leaf has its own independent pattern, it flags too many controls. I’m preserving that result and adding a whole-leaf partner-randomization check before calling the procedure qualified. This matters because words on a manuscript leaf needn’t behave independently. 🗡️🐍

It also misses most weak plants. I’m keeping those misses prominent: good false-positive control won’t make a later negative result evidence that no weak pattern exists.

The final fixture passes too. Across the frozen suite, the combined test flags 6/800 independent-word controls and 24/800 independent-leaf controls, and detects 48/48 strong plants. It finds only 13/48 weak plants, so that sensitivity limit stays attached.

I’ve replayed the saved null scores and decisions and verified that the earlier receipts are unchanged. I’m packaging the diagnosis, both attempts, frozen rules, and failures now; no manuscript scores were rerun. 🐍

items.text:
Found the trap: **the test was borrowing baseline errors.** Similar word-family composition let partners share the model’s mistakes, even with independent choices. The old procedure flagged 14/24 fresh independent controls. 🗡️🐍

The frozen replacement refits under both word shuffles and whole-leaf partner randomizations, requiring both tests to pass:

| Control | Flagged/detected |
|---|---:|
| Independent words | 6/800 |
| Independent leaf states | 24/800 |
| Strong shared-sheet plants | 48/48 |
| Weak plants | 13/48 |

**It passes the frozen control suite**, with explicit exchangeability assumptions. Weak-signal sensitivity remains limited.

Both failed procedures are preserved. **No manuscript scores were rerun.**

[Full report](C:/Users/lewis/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15c3d-56da-7f02-bc15-2522dc396abd/voynich-layout/specificity-controls-v22/report.html) · [Reproduction package](C:/Users/lewis/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15c3d-56da-7f02-bc15-2522dc396abd/voynich-layout/wrong-partner-controls-v22.zip)

items.text: I’ll carry the v20 rule and model choices over unchanged, freeze the hand-1 herbal sheet cohort, and rerun the word-family controls and whole-sheet holdouts. I’ll keep the partner-assisted prediction setup explicit and preserve every failed fold. 🐍

The cohort will be **21 documented ordinary sheets**, fixed before this run. Because they span seven quires, I’ll condition the word-family controls and baseline on quire too.

I’ll also compare the true partner with wrong partners from the same quire. That comparison will hold both sheets out of fitting, so it can distinguish a sheet-specific benefit from simply receiving more text from the same quire.

items.text:
The herbal association remains after word-family and quire controls: corrected p = **.0104** in Takahashi and **.0386** in the First Study Group reading.

The heldout gains are positive, but the prediction test hasn’t passed validation. The failed negative control also gets a nominal p = .0022 for “specificity,” and three of six negative controls get nominal p < .05 there. That makes those prediction p-values unreliable as confirmation; I’m recording them separately from the word-family permutation results.
